Technology stocks firmed Monday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding more than 0.7% while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was up 0.6%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ NVIDIA ( NVDA ) was rising in late Monday trading, posting a nearly 3% gain, after the chipmaker announced a collaborative agreement with the Taiwan Ministry of Science and Technology aimed at advancing the country's artificial intelligence capabilities. The partnership will concentrate on developing supercomputing infrastructure, research collaboration and involving the Deep Learning Institute to help train of Taiwanese developers. the new project also will provide financial support for startups through NVIDIA's inception startup acceleration program as well as advancing artificial intelligence in key vertical markets.
In other sector news:
+ Microsoft ( MSFT ) was trading higher Monday afternoon after the tech giant announced its $7.5 billion, all-stock purchase of GitHub, acquiring the software development platform to help advance its cloud business. Microsoft said corporate vice president Nat Friedman will move to the helm at GitHub while the target company's CEO and co-founder Chris Wanstrath will join the parent company as a "technical fellow" working on strategic software initiatives. The deal should close before the end of the year, with Microsoft planning to use a portion of the $30 billion in available capacity for its stock buyback program for the acquisition. It also is expecting the deal will be accretive to non-GAAP operating income by FY20.
- Dell Technologies ( DVMT ) was back near its Monday break-even mark in late trade, recovering from a nearly 2% mid-morning retreat after the company reported improved Q1 financial results compared with the same quarter last yaer. Net loss for the three months ended May 4 was $1.95 per share over a $2.29 per share net loss during the same quarter last year. Revenue grew to $21.36 billion from $18 billion during the year-ago period, topping the single-analyst call expecting $19.19 billion in quarterly revenue.
- Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ) tumbled Monday, falling almost 4% in recent trading after the cyber-security company issued earnings guidance for its current Q4 trailing Wall Street expectationPalo Alto said it is expecting non-GAAP net income for the three months ending in late July in a range of $1.15 to $1.17 per share, trailing the Capital IQ consensus by at least $0.04 per share. The below-consensus projection upstaged better-than-expected Q3 financial results, with Palo Alto earning $0.99 per share during the three months ended April 30, up from $0.61 per share during the same quarter last year and topping the analyst mean by $0.03 per share. Revenue rose to $567.1 million from $431.8 million in the year-ago period and also beat the $546.4 million analyst mean.
